q: The crew’s mess aboard the submarine USS Thomas A. Edison housed which full-sized acoustic musical instrument?
d: A Steinway upright was installed during construction at the captain’s request and remained aboard until decommissioning in 1983.
evidence: Manufacturer history explicitly describes upright piano installed in crew mess in1961 and aboard through1983; no claim about all submarines or current display location.

q: Which structure on Cockspur Island has a ship-prow shape designed to help it withstand wind and waves?
d: The small brick beacon stands on an islet near the mouth of the Savannah River. Its unusual shape helps it face the water’s battering.
s: National Park Service · Cockspur Island Lighthouse
evidence: NPS ranger transcript states lighthouse shaped like ship prow for wind/wave resistance; avoiding a claim that the entire tower is boat-shaped.

q: The intricate pictures inside nineteenth-century “sailors’ valentines” were typically assembled from what?
d: Many were souvenirs made by artisans in Barbados. Sailors could buy the elaborate gifts for loved ones rather than make them during a voyage.
s: Texas A&M University at Galveston · Sailors’ Valentines
evidence: Institutional maritime account identifies shell designs and local Barbadian artisans selling souvenirs, correcting assumption sailors made them.

q: After losing his right arm, Nelson could eat using a fork fitted with which extra feature?
d: One example in the Greenwich collection has a separate steel blade screwed alongside its three prongs, combining two utensils in one hand.
s: Royal Museums Greenwich · Nelson’s combined knife and fork
evidence: Museum image record describes a separate steel blade attached by screw beside three silver prongs and use after1797 arm loss; does not repeat erroneous Battle of Nile arm-loss dating elsewhere.

q: The clocks aboard the retired Royal Yacht Britannia were stopped at 3:01 p.m. to mark which moment?
d: The time records when Elizabeth II was piped ashore for the last time, making the stopped clocks a permanent farewell.
evidence: Owning trust states all clocks stopped at15:01 at final royal departure; uses history page rather than shop listing with erroneous first-time wording.

q: An evening gown linked to the 1893 Chicago World’s Fair combined silk with threads made from which surprisingly brittle material?
d: Glassblowers drew molten glass into fine filaments that could be woven with silk. The Deutsches Museum has conserved the surviving skirt of Infanta Eulalia’s gown.
evidence: Museum research explains molten glass pulled into fine threads and woven with silk, with surviving skirt conserved; avoids saying glass sculpture or entirely glass garment.

q: A modern replica of an Ainu robe shown by Smithsonian Ocean is sewn from which traditional clothing material?
d: Traditional fish-skin construction is combined with Japanese katazome printing in this modern replica.
evidence: Institution identifies modern Ainu fish-skin replica by Palomino-Perez, Vanna Bellini and Takayuki Ishii, printed with katazome technique.

q: Yup’ik maker Theresa Moses used which part of a seal for a raincoat acquired by the Smithsonian in 2003?
d: The museum lists seal gut among the coat’s materials and records cutting, drying and sewing techniques. The garment carries the Yup’ik term imarnitek.
s: National Museum of the American Indian · Theresa Moses raincoat
evidence: Holding museum catalog lists creator,2003 acquisition,seal gut/intestines,cut/dried/sewn techniques and indigenous termimarnitek; no generalization to every Arctic people.

q: In Aklan’s traditional piña textile craft, what everyday valuables are used in a local method of weighing fibers?
d: Different denominations help measure the material. The weighing practice is part of the handloom tradition described in UNESCO’s heritage record.
evidence: Nomination entry explicitly says fibers weighed with local method involving old coins of different denominations; different fact from published905 pineapple-leaf extraction.
